evidence.excerpt:
Given a requirement whose test plan has one entry
    name: test_retry_gate_runs_when_both_conditions_due
    angle: discrimination
  and a second requirement whose test plan has one entry with
    angle: discriminating   (a misspelling),
When the requirement store's validator checks both requirements,
  And work is generated from the first requirement,
Then the first requirement is accepted and the second is rejected with a
  message naming the entry, the field "angle", and the permitted values,
  which include "discrimination",
  And the generated work's test requirements carry that entry with
    angle: discrimination, and those test requirements conform to the
    schema that governs generated test requirements,
  And the test writer's taught set of test kinds lists "discrimination"
    beside the seven existing kinds, with its distinguishing rule: the test
    goes red under at least

evidence.excerpt:
Given three places that list the permitted test kinds —
    R, the requirement-side list,
    G, the generated-work-side list,
    T, the test writer's taught set —
  and four prepared variants of them:
    V1: "discrimination" present in R, G and T,
    V2: present in R and T, absent from G,
    V3: present in R and G, absent from T,
    V4: present in G and T, absent from R,
When the lockstep check runs against each variant,
Then V1 passes,
  And V2, V3 and V4 each fail, and each failure names the list that lacks
    "discrimination" and the lists that carry it,
  And V2 in particular fails — today's check compares only R with T, so a
    kind dropped from G alone goes unnoticed; after this work it does not,
  And the check compares the full sets of kinds, so a kind present in G but
    in neither R nor T (for example a stray "discriminating") also fails,
    naming G.

source.title: All three lists of test kinds move together, or the lockstep check names the one that did not
